title: Doctor (MBBS → Specialist)

rows.label: MBBS intern
rows.value: ~₹24,000–30,000/month stipend in many government colleges (varies widely; some private colleges pay far less)

rows.label: Junior Resident / Medical Officer
rows.value: ~₹50,000–80,000/month in government roles (e.g., MP JR stipend ₹66,148/month from 2026)

rows.label: MD/MS specialist
rows.value: Grows strongly; super-specialists in private practice can earn crores

pros: Deep meaning and social respect; you help people directly
Very high job security; the doctor shortage keeps demand strong
High earnings later, especially after specialisation
cons: Extremely competitive entry; many students spend 1–3 drop years
10+ years before stable, high income, while friends in other fields are already earning
24–36 hour shifts as a resident, burnout, and violence against doctors in some hospitals
Private MBBS fees can run into crores

competitionReality.signal: 22,79,743 registered for NEET UG 2026 (13.3 lakh female, 9.5 lakh male); ~20 lakh appeared
competitionReality.reality: ~1.37–1.41 lakh MBBS seats for 2026-27, so roughly 1 seat for every 16 registrants

sceneIdeas: An angry relative in the emergency ward
Choosing which of three patients to see first
Your school friend posts their first car while you earn a stipend
